description: Heating and cooking fuels. energyMJ is per unit. Efficiencies are typical appliance values; 0 means not used for that purpose.

records.name: Firewood (mixed hardwood/softwood)
records.notes: Full cord = 128 ft³ (3.62 m³) stacked, air-dried 1 year. Birch/maple/ash run higher; spruce/poplar lower.

records.name: Propane
records.notes: A 100 lb cylinder holds about 90 L. Most furnaces need electricity; plan a direct-vent or vent-free heater. Below −40 °C propane barely vaporizes.

records.name: Kerosene
records.notes: Stores for years. Indoor use needs ventilation and a CO alarm.

records.name: Heating oil
records.notes: Oil furnaces need electricity to run.

records.name: Wood pellets
records.notes: Pellet stoves need electricity for the auger and fan; keep a battery or generator plan.

records.name: Electric
records.notes: Grid-down means no heat. Plan a backup source.

records.name: White gas (camp fuel)
records.notes: Works in deep cold, unlike butane canisters.

records.name: Butane canisters
records.notes: Fails below about 0 °C. Summer or indoor only.
